Do not overwrite without a source that actually states 2.0.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE / START / LENGTH / DIAMETER all corroborate cleanly. The pipeline is real, distinct from every other roster entry (it is Ukraine's only Hust-area export/interconnector line to Romania; no overlap with the Poland spur P0778, Hungary spurs P0780/P1489/P3063, or any Dolyna/Izmail/Dikanka cluster — no duplicate flag). A contemporaneous Interfax-Ukraine wire story (archived via elvisti.com, dated 1999-12-06, accessed live through Wayback since the origin site 403s bots) reports: 'The ceremonial opening of the Ukrainian and Romanian sections of the "Khust-Satu Mare" gas pipeline took place on Dec 2 and 3 [1999] respectively. Pipeline length is 20.6 km, diameter 720mm' — an EXACT match to the sheet's LengthKnown=20.60km and Diameter=720mm, and it dates the 1999 StartYear1 to the week of Dec 2-3, 1999. Independently, Naftogaz's own official corporate-history page (naftogaz.com, current, actively maintained) lists under '1999': 'Ukrtransgaz put into operation the Khust-Satu Mare main gas pipeline to transport up to 4 bcm of natural gas per year to the Romanian market via this route' — confirms existence, name, and 1999 start year from a second, later-compiled, independently-authored source (not simply a reprint of the wire story, though its '4 bcm' figure may trace to the same original 1999 announcement, so I am NOT treating that specific figure as doubly independent). English Wikipedia's 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' article (a live, currently-maintained article discussing the network's status through 2023-2024, i.e. describing the PRESENT-DAY system, not just 1999) lists 'the Khust–Satu Mare pipeline' among the western-corridor/Bratstvo pipelines and states it 'enters to Romania through the Tekove metering station' — a third independent naming that also refines the Romanian endpoint (Tekove/Teceu, in Satu Mare county) consistent with the sheet's EndLocation='Satu Mare'/EndCountryOrArea='Romania'. Classification is correct (transmission-grade interconnector, not a gathering/feeder line — both a 1999 press release and the current Wikipedia network list treat it as a main/trunk line). Attribution: sheet's Owner1='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' 100% is CORRECT per the country's post-2020 rule (TSOU took over from Ukrtransgaz on 2020-01-01) and is independently confirmed by tsoua.com's own 'Key Facts' page, which gives the entity's full legal name as 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, Limited Liability Company' — no Gazprom mis-attribution, no concern. The one open item is Capacity: both 1999-era sources describe the line's PURPOSE/design ceiling as 'up to 4 bcm/y' to Romania, not 2.0 bcm/y as recorded. This could be (a) a genuine sheet error, (b) a distinction between nameplate/design capacity ('up to') and an actually allocated/utilized throughput figure the sheet is tracking, or (c) both 1999 sources tracing to one Ukrtransgaz press release that itself overstated the design ceiling. I could not resolve this with a TSOU technical-capacity document in the time available (web-search budget was exhausted mid-pass), so I am flagging rather than changing the value — do not fill Capacity [ref] with either of these sources since they contradict the stated number.
